text:
Maya (support): heads up — ACME-Pay hit production today, their checkout flow started failing when we switched them to JSON/structured mode. They get a 400 from our API and their parser chokes. Can we triage?

ACME-PM: Our logs show the model returned something like this in the `details` field and our downstream JSON.parse() crashes. This started after a vendor copy-paste of rich text into a line-item description.

ACME-PM: ```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "name": "T-shirt \"Special\" Edition",
      "note": "Size: L\nColor: blue\u2014limited",
      "price": 19.99
    }
  ]
}
```

Maya (support): the important bits — embedded quotes in the name (escaped as `\"Special\"`) and a literal `\\n` newline plus a long dash encoded as `\\u2014`. Their client sees `Unexpected token \" in JSON at position 25`.

Tom (eng): can you paste the exact API request you sent to us (headers + body) and the response body we returned? need to confirm whether the model produced malformed syntax or if our streaming split broke an escape.

ACME-PM: curl request (sanitized):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"mode":"structured","schema":{"items": [{"name":"string","note":"string","price":"number"}]},"prompt":"Generate invoice items for order 123"}'
```

ACME-PM: response body (truncated):

```json
{"id":"resp_123","result":"{\"items\":" + TRUNCATED }
```

Maya (support): so response had a nested JSON string that appears to be chopped at the streaming boundary. They re-run and sometimes it is valid, sometimes there's an unescaped backslash at the boundary. Intermittent.

Jenna (eng-ml): this smells like an encoding/escape stitching bug when we do token streaming + structured mode. If the model emits a backslash near chunk boundary we might be splitting `\\` into `\` + `` which leaves a single backslash before a quote, breaking JSON. Also note non-ascii `\u2014` combined with `\\n` might be double-escaped by the response formatter.

Marco (eng-runtime): @Jenna good call. Can you confirm which model and tokenizer they were routed to? Also need exact streaming chunk sizes and whether we apply any post-processing on each chunk (we do apply JSON-mode escape normalization currently).

Jenna (eng-ml): they were on `redwood-alpha-4k` (hosted). Tokenization of `\\n` vs `\\\n` differs across merges; I'll reproduce with same model and enable debug token boundaries.

Tom (eng): steps I'll take: reproduce locally with curl/streaming, capture raw socket frames, and run our stitcher unit to see where escapes are dropped. ACME provided a repro case with the exact string above, which is good.

Maya (support): customer is blocked on checkout, requesting ETA. They also mentioned they tried switching off structured mode and it worked (they got plain text and could parse manually).

Priya (billing): not a billing incident — they're not on a usage cap. Confirmed.

Marco (eng-runtime): ops-bot shows some 422 parse_failure spikes at ~14:02 UTC for ACME's account across two hosts. log id: host-42:2023-07-14T14:02:13Z parse_error offset=27

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20230714-1222 for parse failures @ host-42; assigned to eng-runtime.

Tom (eng): repro notes for the team:
1) send structured-mode request with `mode=structured` and schema for items.
2) prompt that includes copy-pasted rich text (quotes, `\\n`, long dash).
3) enable streaming (chunk_size=512) and capture each chunk raw.
4) run our stitcher on the chunks and diff against a non-streaming response.

Jenna (eng-ml): quick patch suggestion: ensure we escape a trailing solitary backslash in a chunk by converting a lone `\` at the end of a chunk to `\\` before concatenation, and run the JSON validator only after full assemble. But that is only a mitigation; underlying issue may be model-level emission of escape sequences.

Marco (eng-runtime): agree to mitigation. Will deploy a hotfix to the stitcher for streaming v1 for hosted tier and enable additional logging for `\\` near chunk boundaries. Rolling patch to canary region now.

Maya (support): I told ACME we'll push a fix in the next 2 hours and offered a short-term workaround: disable structured mode or fallback to non-streaming. They accepted. :thumbsup:

ACME-PM: thanks — disabling structured mode works around it for now. Please ping when fixed.

Tom (eng): followups: add unit tests simulating chunk-split on `\\` + `\"`, add fuzzing with unicode escapes, and check our serializer doesn't do double-escape for `\\uXXXX`.

Jenna (eng-ml): also reach out to model-onboarding team to check if any tokenizer updates changed merging behavior last week.

Marco (eng-runtime): patch deployed to canary, ops shows no more parse failures for the canary host. Scheduling full rollout after 30m bake.

Maya (support): will update customer when full rollout completes.

Priya (billing): marking as not-billing.

Tom (eng): postmortem action items: 1) hotfix merged, 2) regression test in streaming harness, 3) telemetry alert for chunk-boundary backslash frequency.

Maya (support): closing loop: ACME confirmed checkout unblocked after full rollout. They asked for a short note we can include in release notes about structured-mode streaming stability.

ACME-PM: appreciated the quick turnaround.
